question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\5&3\end{bmatrix}$, calculate $A^{-1}$. Hence, find the matrix $X$ satisfying $AX=\begin{bmatrix}4\\11\end{bmatrix}$.
explanation:
Determinant of $A$
$$|A|=(2)(3)-(1)(5)=1$$ Since $|A|\ne0$, the inverse exists.
Calculation of the inverse
The adjoint is $$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-5&2\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-5&2\end{bmatrix}$$
Solution of the matrix equation
From $AX=B$, $$X=A^{-1}B$$ Thus, $$X=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-5&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4\\11\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}12-11\\-20+22\end{bmatrix}$$
Required matrix
Hence, $$X=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}$$
